record.title: Brazil’s ANPD consultation analysis maps platform oversight and AI intimate-image proposals
record.summary: On 15 October 2026, Brazil’s data-protection authority (ANPD) published Technical Note 23/2026 analyzing consultation responses on platform regulation under the Marco Civil da Internet. The note says 74 submissions were received and 66 analyzed after screening; participation was led by private-sector contributors (47%), followed by organized civil society (30.3%). ANPD’s synthesis highlights calls for clearer platform-responsibility criteria, proportionate risk-based supervision, transparency reporting and complaint channels, and preventive safeguards against nonconsensual AI-generated intimate content. It also records disagreement over liability criteria, removal deadlines and the limits of agency authority. This is consultation analysis feeding ongoing regulation, not a final binding rule or a representative poll.
organizations: Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD)

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: On 15 October 2026, Brazil’s ANPD published Technical Note 23/2026 analyzing submissions to its 2026 consultation on regulation under the Marco Civil da Internet and Decrees 12.975/2026 and 12.976/2026.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The technical note says the consultation received 74 submissions and analyzed 66 after relevance and duplicate screening; 47% of participation came from the private sector and 30.3% from organized civil society. The note reports submission shares, not representative public opinion.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ANPD’s synthesis reports convergence around clearer platform-responsibility criteria and proportionate, risk-based supervision. Proposed topics include transparency reporting, complaint channels, systemic-failure oversight and preventive measures against nonconsensual AI-generated intimate content. The agency records unresolved disagreements over liability criteria, removal deadlines and the limits of its administrative role.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Technical Note 23/2026 is consultation analysis and input to ongoing agenda and rulemaking work; it does not itself establish final binding platform obligations or show implementation outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: Final binding requirements and agency positions may change after the 2027–2028 agenda consultation and subsequent rulemaking.
No implementation or outcome evidence shows how any eventual platform duties affect safety, expression, privacy or compliance burden.

brief.importance_rationale: If the proposals inform final Brazilian platform rules, they could materially affect platform oversight, reporting, risk management and safeguards for nonconsensual AI-generated intimate content. The note records public consultation analysis rather than adopted obligations, so impact remains prospective and stakeholder input is not a population-representative measure.
limitations: This is ANPD’s synthesis of consultation responses, not an enacted regulation or final agency decision.
The 74 submissions (66 analyzed) are voluntary stakeholder contributions and do not represent public opinion or the full set of affected parties.
Reported alignment does not establish agreement on exact obligations; the note records material disagreements over liability, deadlines and administrative authority.
The note does not measure platform implementation, compliance cost, safety outcomes, impacts on lawful expression or privacy, or the effectiveness of proposed controls.
organizations: Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD)
brief.summary: On 15 October 2026, Brazil’s data-protection authority (ANPD) published Technical Note 23/2026 analyzing consultation responses on platform regulation under the Marco Civil da Internet. The note says 74 submissions were received and 66 analyzed after screening; participation was led by private-sector contributors (47%), followed by organized civil society (30.3%). ANPD’s synthesis highlights calls for clearer platform-responsibility criteria, proportionate risk-based supervision, transparency reporting and complaint channels, and preventive safeguards against nonconsensual AI-generated intimate content. technical.claimed_result: The agency reports 74 submissions, 66 admissible submissions analyzed, and leading themes including general obligations (92%), asymmetric regulatory scope (85%), information/reporting duties (85%) and oversight of systemic platform failures (79%). These percentages describe consultation submissions, not public prevalence.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Portuguese note documents the consultation process, screening counts, agency synthesis and proposed regulatory topics. It records proposals and disagreements; it does not create the final rules.
technical.implementation_status: Regulatory analysis published; the 2027–2028 agenda remained under consultation and future rules were not adopted in this note.
technical.mechanism: ANPD’s Technical Note 23/2026 aggregates responses to 11 consultation questions on the Marco Civil da Internet and Decrees 12.975/2026 and 12.976/2026, grouping convergences, disagreements and proposals to inform its 2027–2028 regulatory agenda and future supervisory rules.
technical.regime: Brazilian data-protection and platform oversight under the Marco Civil da Internet, as amended by Decrees 12.975/2026 and 12.976/2026. Consultation ran 30 June–17 August 2026; the note was published 15 October 2026.
technical.strongest_baseline: No prior final implementing rule or measured compliance outcome is established by this consultation analysis; the comparison is between submitted proposals, areas of reported alignment and recorded disagreements.

brief.title: Brazil’s ANPD consultation analysis maps platform oversight and AI intimate-image proposals
brief.why_it_matters: The consultation analysis shows how Brazil’s regulator is framing implementation of new platform-governance decrees, including supervision of systemic failures and safeguards for AI-generated intimate imagery. If carried into final rules, these issues could affect platform compliance, transparency and content-safety systems in a major Latin American market. The publication records agency synthesis of submissions, not adopted rules or consensus across the broader public.
